description: Overview of major programming languages, their paradigms, and use cases

language_categories.compiled: Source code compiled to machine code before execution (C, C++, Rust, Go)
language_categories.interpreted: Code executed line by line by interpreter (Python, Ruby, JavaScript in browser)
language_categories.jit_compiled: Compiled at runtime (Java via JVM, C# via .NET CLR, JavaScript in V8)
language_categories.scripting: Typically interpreted; automation and glue code (Bash, PowerShell, Python)

python.strengths: Readable syntax, vast ecosystem, rapid prototyping

java.created: 1995 by James Gosling at Sun Microsystems
java.strengths: Platform independence (JVM), strong typing, large ecosystem

c.created: 1972 by Dennis Ritchie at Bell Labs
c.strengths: Close to hardware, maximum performance, portable

rust.strengths: Memory safety without garbage collector; no null pointers

type_systems.static_typing: Types checked at compile time (Java, C++, Rust, TypeScript)
type_systems.dynamic_typing: Types checked at runtime (Python, JavaScript, Ruby)
type_systems.strong_typing: Type coercion rarely happens implicitly (Python, Java)

version_control.git: Most popular VCS; distributed; created by Linus Torvalds 2005
version_control.github: Git hosting + collaboration platform; owned by Microsoft

development_concepts.version_control: Track code changes over time; enable collaboration
development_concepts.ci_cd: Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment; automated build, test, deploy pipelines
development_concepts.agile: Iterative development methodology; sprints, standups, retrospectives
